A1.justification: Despite retitling and substantial reframing, both PDFs describe the same NASA mechanism and SwiftBrush-based distillation work. The main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PG-SB training experiments, HPSv2 and MS-COCO evaluations, guidance ablations, and human-assessed negative-feature removal experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original NASA-T experiments and ablations, NegOpt evaluation, negative-feature removal tests, and CausVid video-generation results.

M1.justification: The original NASA attention rule survives as NASA-I, and randomized teacher guidance survives under SBv2*, rather than being removed with the PG-SB name. However, v3 Section 5.3 introduces NASA-T: negative prompts condition the frozen teacher and NASA-equipped student during distillation, with randomly sampled NASA strength. This substantially extends the procedure beyond v1's inference-only NASA.

E1.justification: v3 adds NegOpt positive/negative prompt pairs, a constructed negative-prompt training dataset, and text-to-video evaluation using CausVid on VBench-Long. The MS-COCO evaluation present in v1 is removed. HPSv2, JourneyDB/LAION training coverage, and the small feature-removal task remain.

E2.justification: The feature-removal comparison adds CFG controls and FLUX.1-schnell while dropping its PG-SB arm (v1 Table 3; v3 Table 2). v3 Table 3 also adds explicit CFG variants to the HPS comparison and omits the original SwiftBrush baseline. The text-embedding-subtraction comparator in v1 Figure 3 is removed. PG-SB becoming SBv2* is a rename, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: v3 introduces evaluation on 30K NegOpt pairs with separate CLIP+ and CLIP− scores and adds VBench-Long aesthetic/imaging metrics, while removing the MS-COCO FID/precision/recall protocol. NASA inference scales change from model-specific values to backbone defaults. Table 6 reports PixArt training at batch 64 for 60K iterations for v1 PG-SB versus batch 32 for 50K iterations for v3 NASA-T; these are different method/settings combinations.

E4.justification: v1's training-stability curves, teacher-CFG sweep and randomized-guidance placement ablation are removed. v3 adds negative-prompt placement ablations across student, teacher and LoRA teacher (Table 5), a quantitative NASA-strength sensitivity curve (Figure 7), and a teacher negative-prompt comparison (Table 1). Qualitative guidance-strength sweeps already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without independent-run counts, seed schedules, confidence intervals or significance tests. The 100-image feature-removal evaluations concern sample size, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many baseline HPS scores survive the renaming, including PixArt PG-SB/SBv2* at 30.34. v3 adds NASA-T results, NegOpt scores, FLUX success rates and video results. Its best HPSv2 score is 31.21 for NASA-T plus NASA-I at alpha=1, versus v1's 31.08 for PG-SB plus NASA at alpha=0.8; this is not a same-setting gain. MS-COCO results and detailed per-prompt success rates are removed.

T1.justification: The diffusion/CFG background and NASA attention equations remain equivalent. v3 Section 5.3 makes a limited formal extension to the VSD formulation by substituting the negative-conditioned frozen-teacher score from Eq. (5). No new theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is supplied; randomized guidance remains specified despite losing its separate displayed gradient.

C1.justification: v1 presents SNOOPI as two contributions: PG-SB training stabilization and inference-time NASA. v3 centers NASA in inference and distillation, newly claiming the first integration of negative prompting into one-step model training and emphasizing minimal computational overhead. PG-SB is no longer a headline novelty claim.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the PG-SB distribution-broadening explanation with an interpretation that negative-conditioned teachers require a correspondingly conditioned student. It revises v1's cross-attention-only applicability boundary through joint-attention FLUX support and discusses video applicability. The scale-tuning caveat remains, but gains a quantitative explanation of deterioration at excessive guidance strength.

D1.justification: The core attention pseudocode, hardware, optimizer, LoRA settings and CLIP-loss details remain. v3 adds negative-prompt construction and NASA-T scale settings and updates training hyperparameters. Conversely, it omits v1's project-page link, exact six-pair human-evaluation protocol and HPS table markers distinguishing cited scores from reruns, reducing reproducibility detail in those areas.

R1.justification: v3 substantially refocuses the related-work discussion from general distillation approaches toward distribution matching and negative prompting. Randomized CFG is now attributed to Flash Diffusion in Section 6.1. New negative-prompt, community-tool, joint-attention and video references support a different research positioning, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around NASA. The PG-SB section is replaced by Observations, the method is reorganized into NASA, NASA-I and NASA-T, and the experiments and appendices are substantially restructured. These are major narrative changes beyond added scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the opening montage and main comparison table, adds FLUX/video illustrations and a quantitative scale plot, and removes the FID curve, MS-COCO table and PG-SB sample galleries. The NASA schematic is retained and relocated from Figure 4 to Figure 3; guidance-sweep material is reorganized and expanded rather than wholly new.

improvement.justification: v3 more directly supports negative-prompt control through large-scale NegOpt evaluation, explicit CFG comparisons, component ablations and quantitative scale analysis. FLUX experiments also address v1's stated architectural limitation. However, removal of detailed human-evaluation procedures and result-provenance markers reduces auditability, while dropping MS-COCO checks narrows fidelity/diversity evidence. The stronger focused validation provides a modest net improvement; the higher headline HPSv2 score is not a controlled before-and-after gain.
